**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Remove the now-unused getBlobs buffer pool**

`getBlobs()` now ignores its `buffers` argument, but `GetBlobsTracker` still allocates and retains one `BLOB_AND_PROOF_V2_RPC_BYTES` buffer per maximum blob for every concurrent recovery slot before passing that argument. Thus any Fulu/Gloas data recovery permanently grows the tracker with large zero-filled buffers that are never used, while the response is separately allocated; remove the pool or stop allocating it when using this non-aliasing path.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
I think this is stale.
Confirmed stale. At 4c98359, `getBlobs` passes `buffers` through to `getBlobsV2`, and the JSON-RPC transport decodes into them. Only the REST transport doesn't use the pool, which is by design.
why would we accept pre-fulu? we should probably just throw early

Yea I think we should. But sim test is complaining if I do it now because it still runs Electra blocks. 

Need to update sim test and throw in a separate PR

Done in 7322e2da4d. publishBlockV2 now throws 400 for any pre-fulu block whose blob commitments are non-empty, before anything is cached. Blob-free pre-fulu blocks still publish, which keeps multiFork/mixedClient (FULU_FORK_EPOCH: Infinity) working. Covered by two new unit tests.
that comment is odd, we could fail explicitly at the start of the function call if it's pre-fulu, I prefer that over silently producing an invalid result

Agree. One constraint: `multiFork.test.ts` and `mixedClient.test.ts` still run with `FULU_FORK_EPOCH: Infinity`, and their Lodestar validators publish electra blocks through `publishBlockV2`, so a plain pre-fulu throw would fail both sims. Throwing only when pre-fulu contents carry blobs (`blobs.length > 0`) keeps the sims working, since they never send blob transactions. It also fails loudly instead of publishing a block whose blobs no peer will get.

Comment dropped and replaced by an explicit throw at the top of the function, see 7322e2da4d. It keys on the block's blob commitments rather than the supplied blobs, so an electra block with commitments but an empty blobs array is rejected too instead of being imported without data.
why is this fork guarded? don't we only run sim tests post fulu anyways?

Not yet. `multiFork.test.ts` sets `FULU_FORK_EPOCH: Infinity` and calls `assertUnknownBlockSync` (L158), so the head here is an electra block. With this PR, pre-fulu `getBlobSidecars` reads the blob DB, which nothing writes anymore, so it 404s for every electra block and the sim fails without the guard. Once the sims run post-fulu, the guard can go.

multiFork still runs electra heads (FULU_FORK_EPOCH: Infinity) and calls assertUnknownBlockSync, and pre-fulu blobs are no longer in the DB, so the API would 404 without the guard. Kept it with a one-line comment. It can go once the sims run post-fulu.
we should use `getBlobs` instead of `getBlobSidecars`

Agree. That change also needs proofs: `getBlobs` returns blobs without them, and fulu `publishBlockV2` reads `kzgProofs` as 128 cell proofs per blob. The current `currentSidecars.map((b) => b.kzgProof)` passes one blob proof per blob, which would already be wrong for a fulu head with blobs. It's only never hit because no sim sends blob transactions. So with `getBlobs` the cell proofs need computing, for example with `kzg.computeCellsAndKzgProofs(blob).proofs`.

Switched to getBlobs in 7322e2da4d. Since fulu publishBlockV2 slices kzgProofs as NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS per blob, the util now computes cell proofs with kzg.computeCellsAndKzgProofs instead of passing one blob proof per blob, which was already wrong for a fulu head with blobs.

Agree. One line is enough, for example `# Pre-fulu blob sidecar functions, replaced by data columns in fulu` above the deneb entries. The electra comment pointing back to it can then go.
